file_purpose: Condition-aware exercise recommendation configuration for the mobility monitoring chatbot.
global_safety_message: Suggested exercises must come from a clinician-approved care plan. The chatbot may explain and display approved exercises but must not diagnose, prescribe, change dosage, or create patient-specific treatment targets.

knee_rehabilitation.description: Exercises related to controlled knee movement and functional lower-limb activity.

lower_limb_strength_and_control.description: Exercises involving coordinated hip, knee, ankle, and trunk movement.

balance_and_stepping.description: Exercises involving single-leg support, stepping, foot clearance, and balance.

lateral_mobility.description: Exercises emphasizing controlled side-to-side lower-limb movement.

squat_movement_training.description: Exercises involving controlled lowering and return to standing.

general_lower_limb_mobility.description: Fallback profile used only when a clinician-approved patient condition mapping is unavailable.

purpose: Represent a squat movement for posture and consistency analysis
Support explanations of alignment and controlled descent
starting_position: Stand using the stance specified by the care team
Keep the feet stable on the floor
Begin with an upright, controlled trunk position

movement_phases.description: The hips and knees flex as the body moves downward.
The lowest configured position is reached while alignment is maintained.
The hips and knees extend as the body returns to standing.

common_execution_errors.safe_explanation: The knees may not have remained aligned with the feet.
The trunk may have leaned forward more than expected.

observable_signals: reduced knee or hip flexion relative to configured target
common_execution_errors.safe_explanation: The movement may not have reached the configured target depth.
The heels may not have remained in stable contact with the floor.

patient_friendly_guidance: Use only the depth assigned by the care team.
Keep the feet stable and the knees aligned with the feet.
Keep the trunk controlled.
Move down and up smoothly.
safety_notes: This record does not define a safe squat depth for a specific patient.
Use assistance or supervision when required.
Stop for severe pain, sudden weakness, dizziness, or loss of balance.

care_plan_parameters.notes: Values must come from the patient's clinician-approved care plan.

purpose: Represent a stepping movement involving single-leg support
Support balance and lower-limb alignment analysis
starting_position: Stand in the setup specified by the care team
Maintain a stable trunk before stepping

movement_phases.description: Body weight shifts onto the supporting leg.
The moving leg lifts and passes over the obstacle.
The foot is placed while balance is maintained.
The user returns to the starting position with control.

observable_signals: hip, knee, or ankle moving out of vertical alignment
common_execution_errors.safe_explanation: The supporting leg may not have remained aligned during the step.
The trunk may have moved sideways to compensate for balance.

observable_signals: low foot clearance relative to obstacle
common_execution_errors.safe_explanation: The moving foot may not have cleared the obstacle by the configured margin.
The movement may have required an unexpected balance correction.

patient_friendly_guidance: Use support when assigned.
Move slowly and keep the supporting leg stable.
Lift the stepping foot only as high as required.
Return to the starting position with control.
safety_notes: The obstacle height and support requirements must come from the care plan.
This exercise may create a fall risk and should not be attempted without required supervision.
Stop after a near-fall, fall, severe pain, or sudden weakness.

care_plan_parameters.notes: Values must come from the patient's clinician-approved care plan.

purpose: Represent controlled knee-extension movement for dashboard explanations
Describe observable movement phases without prescribing treatment
starting_position: Sit in a stable chair with the back supported when appropriate
Keep the thigh supported and the trunk steady
Begin with the knee flexed and the foot in a comfortable resting position
Follow the range and duration configured by the care team

movement_phases.description: The leg remains near the starting position before movement begins.
The lower leg moves forward and upward as the knee extends.
The target position is maintained for the configured duration, when a hold is part of the care plan.
The lower leg returns gradually to the starting position.

common_execution_errors.safe_explanation: The lower leg may not have reached the configured target position.
The movement may have been performed faster or less smoothly than expected.
The raised position was not maintained for the configured duration.
The upper body or thigh may have moved to compensate during the exercise.

patient_friendly_guidance: Sit upright and keep the thigh steady.
Raise the lower leg smoothly.
Use only the range and hold time assigned by the care team.
Lower the leg slowly and with control.
safety_notes: This guide is educational and does not prescribe a patient-specific range of motion.
Stop and seek appropriate help for severe pain, sudden weakness, dizziness, a fall, or loss of balance.
Target angles, repetitions, resistance, and hold times must come from the care plan or clinician.

purpose: Represent controlled lateral stepping and lowering
Support alignment, symmetry, and balance analysis
starting_position: Stand using the stance specified by the care team

movement_phases.description: One foot steps to the side.
The body lowers toward the stepping side as the hip and knee flex.
The user pushes through the stepping leg and returns to the starting position.

observable_signals: knee moving inward or away from foot alignment
common_execution_errors.safe_explanation: The knee may not have remained aligned with the foot.

observable_signals: large lateral or forward trunk angle
common_execution_errors.safe_explanation: The trunk may have leaned more than expected during the movement.
The side step or return may have been less controlled than expected.

patient_friendly_guidance: Use only the step width and depth assigned by the care team.
Keep the knee aligned with the foot.
Keep the trunk controlled.
Return to the starting position smoothly.
safety_notes: The chatbot must not prescribe step width, depth, or repetition count.
Stop for severe pain, sudden weakness, dizziness, or loss of balance.

care_plan_parameters.notes: Values must come from the patient's clinician-approved care plan.

purpose: Represent the transition between sitting and standing
Support posture, balance, and repetition analysis
Describe observable movement features for chatbot explanations
starting_position: Sit on a stable chair using the setup specified by the care team
Place the feet in a stable position
Keep the trunk controlled before initiating the movement

movement_phases.description: The user prepares to rise while maintaining a stable seated position.
The trunk moves forward to shift body weight over the feet.
The hips and knees extend as the body rises from the chair.
The user reaches a stable upright position.
The hips and knees flex as the user returns to the chair with control.

observable_signals: knees moving inward or outward relative to feet
common_execution_errors.safe_explanation: The knees may not have remained aligned with the feet during the movement.
The upper body may have moved more than expected to assist the transition.
More weight may have been placed on one side than the other.
The return to the chair may have been faster or less controlled than expected.

patient_friendly_guidance: Use the chair and foot placement assigned by the care team.
Shift forward in a controlled way before standing.
Keep the knees aligned with the feet.
Return to the chair slowly and with control.
safety_notes: Use support or supervision when required by the care plan.
Do not perform the exercise if the environment is unstable or unsafe.
Stop and seek help after a fall, severe pain, sudden weakness, dizziness, or loss of balance.
